scope: Restored Wannsee villa exterior: hipped tiled roof with eyebrow dormer, columned street facade, lake-facing pediment and loggia, shutters and raised terrace. Exclude the wider garden and separate garden house.

facts: Two-storey symmetrical plaster house on natural-stone base, with hipped roof and timber shutters.
Street facade: monumental Ionic columns in a two-storey loggia, with wide eyebrow dormer above.
Lake facade: pediment and pilasters over three central window axes; left loggia repeats the street column motif.
Secondary side entrance has a small column-supported pergola; fine position/dimensions remain unresolved.
Conservation and conversion to a museum took place in2003–06.

sources.publisher: Nina Nedelykov and Pedro Moreira, restoring architects
sources.title: Eine kurze Baugeschichte der Liebermann-Villa (2014)
facts: Final November1909design simplified earlier rejected roof/projection proposals to a cubically reduced body and plain hipped roof.
Lake side has seven window axes, with tall ground-floor garden doors and low upper sills.
Rough sand-coloured plaster, stone base and continuous smooth cornice, pale sandstone surrounds, shell-limestone elements, white window frames and greenish timber shutters.
Side window arrangement follows internal room functions and is not strictly symmetrical.

facts: Street facade has two monumental shell-limestone columns; lake side has a pedimented central projection.
House and garden were restored for museum opening in2006.
Upper lake-facing terrace extends the living space; wider gardens and separate garden house remain outside this model scope.
